verses.text: On the third day, a wedding was going down in Cana, Galilee. Jesus’ mom was there.
Jesus and his disciples got the invite too.
The wine ran out, and Jesus’ mom told him, “They’re out of wine.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with us? My time hasn’t come yet.”
His mother told the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
Six stone water jars were sitting there for the Jewish purification custom. Each one held two or three metretes.
Jesus told the servants, “Fill those jars with water.” They filled every one right to the brim.
Then he said, “Now scoop some out and take it to the feast manager.” So they did.
The feast manager tasted the water—it had turned into wine. He didn’t know where it came from, but the servants who drew the water knew. So he called the bridegroom over
and said, “Everybody serves the good wine first. Once the guests have had plenty, then they bring out the cheaper stuff. But you’ve kept the best till now!”
This was Jesus’ first sign, done in Cana of Galilee. He showed his glory, and his disciples put their faith in him. ✨
After that, Jesus went down to Capernaum with his mom, brothers, and disciples. They stayed there a few days.
The Jewish Passover was close, so Jesus headed up to Jerusalem.
Inside the temple, he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, while money changers sat at their tables.
He made a whip from cords and drove them all out—the sheep and cattle too. He scattered the money changers’ coins and flipped their tables.
He told the dove sellers, “Get all this out of here! Don’t turn my Father’s house into a marketplace!”
His disciples remembered the Scripture that says, “Passion for your house will consume me.”
The Jewish leaders challenged him: “What sign can you show us for doing all this?”
Jesus answered, “Tear down this temple, and I’ll raise it in three days.”
They said, “This temple took forty-six years to build, and you’re saying you’ll raise it in three days?”
But Jesus was talking about the temple of his body.
After Jesus rose from the dead, his disciples remembered he’d said this. They believed the Scripture and what Jesus had told them.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for Passover, lots of people believed in his name because they saw the signs he was doing.
But Jesus didn’t put his trust in them, because he knew everybody.
He didn’t need anyone to fill him in about people. He already knew what was going on inside them.
